name: Barney Stinson
why: Barney's suited-up bar persona runs on Scotch, the 'Glen McKenna' single malt is his marker of manufactured sophistication.

name: Bridget Jones
why: Bridget's diary counts the units of Chardonnay as faithfully as the cigarettes, the large glass of white is her comfort and her downfall.

name: Captain Haddock
why: Hergé's sea captain is devoted to Loch Lomond whisky, a running gag whenever his bottle runs dry mid-adventure.

name: Captain Jack Sparrow
why: Sparrow's love of rum is a running thread of the films, 'But why is the rum gone?', the pirate's fuel and lament.
howToOrder: Rum. And don't let it run out.

name: Carrie Bradshaw
why: The Cosmo is Carrie and the girls' signature Manhattan order, the pink vodka-cranberry cocktail SATC turned into a late-'90s phenomenon.

name: Del Boy (Derek Trotter)
why: Del Boy's social-climbing order at the wine bar is a string of mispronounced cocktails, a 'Piña Colada' and invented tipples like a 'Caribbean Stallion'.
howToOrder: A Piña Colada, and one for the ladies.

name: Don Draper
why: Draper's drink of choice in 'Mad Men' is the Old Fashioned, he even makes one on screen, muddling sugar and bitters over rye.

name: Fleabag
why: Fleabag's default order across the series is a gin and tonic, the drink she nurses through the show's fourth-wall-breaking confessionals.
howToOrder: A gin and tonic. A double.

name: Francis Begbie
why: Begbie holds court over pints in the pub, memorably lobbing an empty pint glass over the balcony to start a brawl.

name: Frasier & Niles Crane
why: The fastidious Crane brothers unwind over glasses of sherry, the fussy fortified wine that became a running signifier of their highbrow pretension.

name: Gandalf
why: Tolkien's wizard has a hobbit-like fondness for the Shire's ale and, best of all, a bottle of the fine red 'Old Winyards', plus his beloved pipe-weed.
sourceName: The Lord of the Rings (J.R.R. Tolkien)
howToOrder: A glass of the Old Winyards.

name: Hawkeye Pierce
why: Hawkeye and Trapper distil their own gin in the Swamp to make martinis, his dry, wisecracking antidote to the war around him.

name: Homer Simpson
why: Homer's beloved brand throughout 'The Simpsons' is Duff, pulled at Moe's Tavern, 'To alcohol! The cause of, and solution to, all of life's problems.'

name: James Bond
why: In 'Casino Royale' Bond invents the Vesper: 'Three measures of Gordon's, one of vodka, half a measure of Kina Lillet... shaken very well until it's ice-cold.'
howToOrder: A dry martini, shaken, not stirred.

name: Jay Gatsby
why: Gatsby's West Egg parties float on rivers of champagne, the drink of his dazzling, doomed reinvention (though he himself barely drinks).

name: Lorelai Gilmore
why: Lorelai runs on coffee, endless cups at Luke's Diner, 'I can't stop drinking the coffee. If I stop drinking the coffee, I stop doing the standing and the walking.'

name: Norm Peterson
why: Norm's entire arc at 'Cheers' is the perpetual barstool pint, the answer to 'What'll you have, Normie?' is always another beer.

name: Olivia Pope
why: Pope decompresses with an enormous glass of red wine and popcorn, a signature 'Scandal' image of the fixer off duty.
howToOrder: A very large glass of red.

name: Patsy Stone & Edina Monsoon
why: Ab Fab's hedonists live on 'Bolly', Bollinger champagne, chased with 'Stoli', slurring 'Bolly, sweetie?' from morning onward.

name: Rick Blaine
why: The jaded owner of Rick's Café Américain drinks bourbon alone after hours, 'Of all the gin joints in all the towns in all the world, she walks into mine.'
howToOrder: Bourbon. Here's looking at you, kid.

name: Roger Sterling
why: Sterling's day-drinking wit is fuelled by vodka, the near-odourless spirit that lets the ad man stay sharp-tongued from lunch onward.
howToOrder: A vodka. It's past noon somewhere.

name: Ron Burgundy
why: In 'Anchorman', Ron Burgundy downs a glass of milk during a sweltering street brawl and deadpans 'Milk was a bad choice' as the heat gets to him.
sourceName: Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy

name: Ron Swanson
why: Ron drinks Lagavulin 16 neat, the peaty Islay single malt he loves so much the show sent him to tour the distillery.
howToOrder: Lagavulin. Neat. And your finest steak.

name: Sir John Falstaff
why: Shakespeare's fat knight delivers a whole speech in praise of 'sherris-sack', the sweet fortified wine he insists warms the blood and sharpens the wit.

name: The Dude (Jeffrey Lebowski)
why: The Dude sips White Russians, 'Caucasians', throughout the film, mixing them wherever he finds cream, even from a half-and-half.

name: Thomas Shelby
why: The Birmingham gang boss is rarely without a tumbler of neat whiskey, poured through the smoke and scheming of 'Peaky Blinders'.

name: Tony Soprano
why: The New Jersey mob boss talks business over a heavy tumbler of Scotch, often single malt, poured at the Bada Bing or his own kitchen.

name: Tyrion Lannister
why: Tyrion's constant companion is a cup of red wine, 'That's what I do: I drink and I know things.'

name: Withnail
why: The permanently soused actor demands 'the finest wines available to humanity', and, in extremis, downs a can of lighter fluid.
howToOrder: The finest wine available to humanity. And a pair of pale ales.

name: Action Bronson
why: Bronson is an evangelist for natural wine, devoting a Vice series to hunting down the best low-intervention bottles in Paris.
howToOrder: Something natural, orange if you've got it.

name: Adele
why: Adele, who wrote 'I Drink Wine', has named wine among her favourite drinks and planned to mark the end of her Vegas residency by opening a special bottle.

name: Adolphus Busch
why: The man who made Budweiser a national brand privately called his own beer 'dot schlop' and preferred to drink wine.
howToOrder: A glass of wine, whatever is good.

name: Andrew Zimmern
why: The adventurous-eating host loves grapefruit La Croix so much he orders the sparkling water by the case.

name: Anthony Bourdain
why: The globe-trotting chef called the Negroni 'the perfect drink': 'three liquors I'm not particularly interested in, but put them together with a slice of orange... it works.'

name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
why: Back in Austria he ends a hike with a radler, beer cut with lemonade, which he calls really refreshing.
howToOrder: A radler: half lager, half lemonade.

name: Arthur Guinness
why: He signed a 9,000 year lease on St James's Gate in 1759, switched to brewing the dark English style called porter in the 1770s, and by 1799 had given up ale entirely to bet the brewery on it.

name: Barack Obama
why: Obama became the first president to brew beer at the White House, buying the kit himself; the honey ale used honey from the South Lawn hives.

name: Bethenny Frankel
why: She invented it for herself at a bar in 2008, reciting the recipe on camera as 'Patron silver on the rocks, fresh lime juice and a little splash of triple sec', then built a company on it.
howToOrder: Tequila on the rocks with fresh lime and a splash of triple sec.

name: Betty White
drink: Vodka on the rocks with lemon
why: America's favourite grandmother 'loved drinking vodka on ice' with, in her words, 'lots and lots of lemon', often with chocolate cake for breakfast.
howToOrder: Vodka on the rocks, lots of lemon.

name: Bill Gates
why: Gates is such a Diet Coke devotee he reportedly turned down a $300 Michelin tasting menu in favour of one, and sips it through podcast interviews.

name: Bill Murray
why: 'He prefers vodka', Murray loves it so much he put his own money into a vodka brand, and swears by a hangover trick of champagne poured over ice.

name: Blake Lively
why: 'I don't drink', she said launching Betty Buzz, after years of mixing but not drinking cocktails convinced her mixers deserved as much love as the spirits.
howToOrder: Sparkling grapefruit over ice, no alcohol.

name: Bob Dylan
why: He co-founded Heaven's Door out of a long-standing love of American whiskey, saying he wanted a collection of whiskeys that 'in their own way, tell a story'.

name: Bob Iger
why: The 4am routine he credits for running Disney starts with coffee, then an hour of exercise, before anything else happens.

name: Charlie Munger
why: Weeks before he died at 99 he told CNBC: 'I drink Diet Coke. I'm sure Diet Coke shortens my life a little. But I don't give a damn.'

name: Coco Chanel
why: Staying at the Savoy she drank red wine and ate caviar, in the belief that the combination kept her looking young.

name: Cristiano Ronaldo
why: At Euro 2020 he pushed two Coca-Cola bottles aside, held up a water and said 'Agua!', a viral moment reflecting his teetotal, water-first diet.

name: Danny DeVito
why: DeVito 'loves Limoncello so much', after slurring through an Oscars appearance on it, that he launched his own brand of the Italian lemon liqueur.

name: David Beckham
why: Beckham told GQ he's 'happy to have a pint anywhere in the world', an easy-going love of beer he later fronted a Stella Artois campaign around.

name: Dolly Parton
why: Parton has named red wine her go-to travelling tipple, her 'favorite plane drink', and has since launched her own Dolly Wine label.

name: Dwayne Johnson
why: He built Teremana to be the tequila he actually wanted to pour, and says it let him 'strip it all away and say, let's just have a drink and talk'.

name: Ed Sheeran
why: Asked his favourite beer, the Suffolk-raised singer 'plumped for Earl Soham Brewery's Victoria Bitter', calling it 'great' and pointing fans to The Station pub in Framlingham.

name: Elizabeth Taylor
why: Old Hollywood's Taylor was 'a whiskey girl' whose favourite was Jack Daniel's, she'd happily pair it with a plate of crispy fried chicken.

name: Elon Musk
why: Musk says he dislikes most alcohol and declared 'Diet Coke is still my fav drink', preferring the caffeine-free version.

name: Emma Chamberlain
why: Chamberlain turned her genuine coffee obsession into Chamberlain Coffee, and still reaches for a mocha latte as her everyday cup.

name: Ernest Hemingway
why: At El Floridita in Havana Hemingway drank his daiquiris double and sugarless, the 'Papa Doble' with extra rum, grapefruit and maraschino.
howToOrder: A Papa Doble, daiquiri, double rum, no sugar.

name: Frank Sinatra
drink: Jack Daniel's with ice and water
why: Ol' Blue Eyes drank Jack Daniel's so devotedly a bottle was buried with him; his exact serve was three ice cubes, two fingers of Jack and a splash of water.
howToOrder: Jack Daniel's, three cubes, two fingers, splash of water.

name: Freddie Mercury
why: Per his PA Peter Freestone, Mercury's evening drink was a vodka tonic made strictly with Stolichnaya, he'd tour with a dry-ice cooler of Stoli.

name: George Clooney
why: His search for 'the perfect Tequila' with Rande Gerber became Casamigos, which the friends drink 'on the rocks, by the shot, at times straight from the bottle'.

name: Gordon Ramsay
why: On Fallon, Ramsay named his favourite cocktail the aptly-insulting 'Wake Up, You Donkey', tequila with cider, honey and smoked elderflower, declaring it delicious.

name: Guy Fieri
why: He calls the bitter Italian amaro 'a great digestivo', keeps a bottle in every fridge and freezer he owns, and is happy to drink it warm.

name: Harry Styles
why: Styles is partial to neat tequila, memorably handing Lizzo a wine glass of it at the 2020 Brit Awards, which she promptly downed.

name: Howard Schultz
why: His morning order is a double espresso macchiato, and every year before the annual meeting he drinks a doppio macchiato at the original Pike Place store.

name: Hunter S. Thompson
why: Thompson's Wild Turkey intake was 'legendary', the high-proof bourbon was a fixture of his gonzo routine alongside Chivas and margaritas.

name: Idris Elba
why: Elba quit beer to stay lean and keeps it 'pretty simple' with spirits, favouring gin, a taste he later bottled as his own Porter's Gin.

name: James Watt
why: He still calls the beer he first brewed in 2007 'my goto IPA', the one he returns to when he wants to re-affirm what an IPA should taste like.

name: Jamie Oliver
why: He calls the Negroni one of his favourite drinks and 'an absolute classic, using three different boozes', and has published a shelf of variations on it.
howToOrder: A Negroni, with an orange twist.

name: Jay-Z
why: He bought the Ace of Spades champagne house outright in 2014 before selling half to LVMH, making it the bottle he built a business around and drinks on camera.
howToOrder: A glass of champagne. Ace of Spades if you have it.

name: Jeff Bezos
why: His morning is built around it: newspaper, black coffee, breakfast with the kids, before any meeting gets booked.

name: Jennifer Aniston
why: Aniston's favourite cocktail is a classic margarita, she's shared her own 'cleaner' version made with tequila, lime and a splash of orange.

name: Jennifer Lawrence
why: 'The biggest actress in Hollywood' outed herself on Conan as a Budweiser gal, popping a beer to celebrate at her own premiere.

name: Jim Koch
why: He drinks his own lager professionally and famously takes a teaspoon of brewer's yeast before a session, a trick he told Esquire keeps him level all night.

name: Judi Dench
why: Dame Judi sums her life up as 'trees and champagne', and has confessed to a secret onstage supper of 'lobster and champagne' during a Shakespeare play.

name: Keith Floyd
why: Floyd pioneered drinking on cookery television, glass of wine permanently in hand, 'I like cooking with wine; sometimes I even put it in the food.'
howToOrder: A glass of wine, for cooking, of course.

name: Keith Richards
why: For decades his road drink was Rebel Yell bourbon, usually cut with a mixer, until he told the press in 2018 he'd 'got fed up with it' and mostly quit.

name: Kevin O'Leary
knownFor: Investor and O'Leary Fine Wines founder
why: 'I don't smoke, I don't do drugs, but I love wine', he says, and the Chardonnay under his own label is the one he sells and drinks.

name: Kim Kardashian
why: Kardashian's 'all-time favorite cocktail' is the lychee martini at Nobu, a sweet sake-and-vodka martini she orders when she dines there.

name: Kingsley Amis
why: In 'Everyday Drinking' Amis set down his signature cocktail, the Lucky Jim, a heavily vodka-forward martini variant cut with cucumber juice.

name: Kylie Minogue
why: Her wine label started with a Provence rose and her Prosecco Rose became the UK's best selling branded Prosecco Rose; she says she drinks across the range for different moods.

name: Lady Gaga
why: Gaga has professed 'undying love' for Jameson and credited the Irish whiskey with helping her write songs: 'I'll drink to that.'

name: Larry Ellison
why: He avoids alcohol on principle, telling his biographer 'I can't stand anything that clouds my mind', and sticks to green tea and carrot juice instead.

name: Lemmy Kilmister
why: For roughly 40 years his constant companion was Jack Daniel's with Coke, a habit so fixed it defined his hell-raising image before doctors moved him to vodka.

name: Marco Pierre White
why: He rejects rigid pairing rules and drinks what he likes: 'I like my game pie, I like my game with a pint of ale. I like my roast pheasant cooked in apples with a pint of cider.'

name: Martha Stewart
why: She has repeatedly named the caipirinha as probably her favourite cocktail, alongside the very dry vodka 'Martha-tini' she orders at a bar.

name: Matthew McConaughey
why: A lifelong Wild Turkey drinker, McConaughey became the brand's creative director and worked with distiller Eddie Russell on his 'perfect bourbon', Longbranch.

name: Nick Offerman
why: Offerman has been 'obsessed with Lagavulin' for over twenty years, a personal love of the peaty Islay malt that long predates his partnership with the distillery.

name: Nigella Lawson
why: Lawson calls the Negroni Sbagliato her ultimate cocktail, a lighter Negroni that swaps the gin for prosecco.
howToOrder: A Negroni Sbagliato, with prosecco in it.

name: Noel Gallagher
why: Ahead of Oasis's reunion Gallagher revealed his 'underwhelming' pre-show order is simply a gin and tonic, a step up from the band's early Guinness-and-JD days.

name: Oliver Reed
why: The legendary hellraiser lived by a line he delivered as Athos in 'The Three Musketeers': 'Life is so much more rosy when seen through the bottom of a glass of ale.'
howToOrder: A pint of ale. And another.

name: Oprah Winfrey
why: Told CNN, with Charles Barkley backing her up, 'I can out tequila almost anyone!', while conceding she is largely off the sauce these days.

name: Post Malone
why: 'It's no secret Post Malone loves a good Bud Light', a genuine attachment he turned into repeated Super Bowl ads and a lager he drinks with his buds.

name: Prince Philip
why: The Duke of Edinburgh's reported favourite beer was Boddingtons, the Manchester 'Cream of the North' ale, a notably down-to-earth royal tipple.

name: Queen Elizabeth II
why: The Queen's reported pre-lunch favourite was a Dubonnet and gin, two parts Dubonnet to one of gin over lots of ice with a lemon slice.
howToOrder: Dubonnet and gin, two to one, lots of ice.

name: Richard Branson
why: Branson's daily routine famously runs on about 20 cups of English Breakfast tea, 'the fuel', he says, for a long working day.

name: Ricky Gervais
why: A self-declared 'big fan of beer', Gervais gave a Vancouver brewery a Golden Globes-night shout-out, calling their lager the best beer he'd ever tasted.

name: Rod Stewart
why: Stewart happily admits he 'loves drinking Appletinis', and gargles a swig of rum and coke before every show as a decades-old pre-stage ritual.

name: Ryan Reynolds
why: He bought into Aviation because, in his words, he loves the taste of it more than any other spirit, and the martini is the serve he pushes hardest.
howToOrder: A gin martini, with a twist.

name: Sam Galsworthy
drink: Dry gin martini with a twist
why: The gin he grew up on ends up in one glass: a dry martini with a twist, and the version he rates most is the sub-zero pour at Dukes in St James's.
howToOrder: A dry gin martini, with a twist.

name: Snoop Dogg
why: His 1993 anthem 'Gin and Juice' made the two-ingredient highball his lifelong calling card, and he still sips it 'laid back' with Tanqueray.
howToOrder: Gin and juice, easy on the ice.

name: Stanley Tucci
why: Tucci's lockdown Negroni demo went viral and cemented the equal-parts aperitivo as his signature, though he insists on a heavier pour of gin.

name: Steve Jobs
why: His fruitarian phases ran on juice: he stocked the Macintosh offices with Odwalla carrot and orange juice and drank so much carrot juice his skin turned faintly orange.

name: Steve Wozniak
why: Asked at BDL Accelerate what he drinks, he said unsweetened iced tea, not the apple juice everyone expects of him.

name: Taylor Swift
why: The Washington Post named the French Blonde, gin, elderflower, Lillet and grapefruit, Taylor Swift's favourite cocktail, 'one for the eras'.

name: Tim Martin
why: He told The Caterer his favourite pint of the moment was Leffe Blond and Doom Bar, having switched off Abbot Ale after Greene King's chief executive campaigned against binge drinking.

name: Tom Holland
why: He stopped drinking in January 2022 and founded Bero because he missed having something good to hold: 'had I had Bero, I think it would have been easier'.

name: Tony Hsieh
why: Fernet was his signature pour and a downtown Las Vegas welcome ritual: 'When new people come to town, we take them to the Downtown Cocktail Room and give their first introductory shot.'

name: Usain Bolt
why: The world's fastest man says he loves 'nothing more than kicking back with a pint of Guinness', and even credited the stout with Red Bull for early speed.

name: Warren Buffett
why: Buffett drinks about five Cokes a day and jokes he owes his health to 'Cherry Coke and hamburgers'; Berkshire is a major Coca-Cola shareholder.

name: Willie Nelson
why: The man who recorded 'Whiskey River' long paired whiskey with weed, though he has since eased off the bottle in favour of the latter.

name: Winston Churchill
why: Churchill's lifelong love was Pol Roger champagne, 'in victory I deserve it, in defeat I need it', backed by weak whisky-and-sodas through the day.

name: Wolfgang Puck
why: He was converted by Burgundy at eighteen in France, and names Chateau Cheval Blanc as his favourite wine of all time: he isn't sure he has tasted anything more amazing.
